_comment: One corpus, two implementations. `shareTokenFromSegment` in apps/mobile/features/share/share.ts and `shareTokenFrom` in infra/router/src/preview.ts read the same URL shape in two deployments that cannot import each other, so they are held the way two copies of a rule are always held here: by running both over these shapes rather than by trusting the comment between them. Add a case here and both suites pick it up. ONE ASYMMETRY IS KNOWN AND NOT FIXED HERE: the router reads a raw `URL.pathname` while the app receives a segment expo-router has already percent-decoded, so the `%` cases below are refused by the router because `%` is outside its charset and by the app because the raw fixture string still contains one — production would hand the app `a-b-<64hex>`, which it would resolve. The direction is fail-closed for disclosure (the note opens, the card stays generic), so it is a broken unfurl rather than a leak; it is stated here because a case that passes for two different reasons reads as coverage and is not. AND CI ONLY RUNS ONE SIDE ON A CHANGE TO THIS FILE: it lives under `infra/router/**`, which triggers the router suite, while the mobile job is gated on `apps/mobile/**` and is skipped. Run `npx jest __tests__/shareViewer.test.ts` in `apps/mobile` by hand when you edit this — see the note in `preview.test.ts` for why importing the app's parser here does not work.

cases.why: a bare token, the shape every link minted before slugs was
a readable slug in front of it
a one-character slug
a slug with a run of doubled separators
digits in the slug
a slug that is itself hex — only the tail is ever read as a token
the token is read off the end, so a leading token is just slug
uppercase hex is not a token
63 characters is not a token
65 characters is not a token
a hyphen with no slug in front of it
a token with nothing after its separator
a slug and no token
an underscore is not slug material
nor is a space
nor a dot, which is how a path segment stops being one
nor a slash
nor a percent escape
the empty segment
a doubled leading hyphen is not slug material either — the charset starts alphanumeric, and relaxing it to [A-Za-z0-9-]+ passed every check before this case existed
a percent-escaped hyphen stays escaped — the router reads a raw pathname and its charset has no %, so this must not resolve
lowercase too, because a case-insensitive decode would be a difference between the two copies
a percent-escaped hex digit inside the token is not the token
a Unicode hyphen lookalike (U+2010) is not the separator
nor a fullwidth one (U+FF0D)
